chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi'a, from Muhammad ibn 'Idhafir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was on one of his journeys, a group of riders met him. They said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.' He turned to them and said: 'Who are you?' They said: 'Believers.' He said: 'Then what is the reality/truth of your faith?' They said: 'Contentment with God's decree, submission to God's command, and entrusting matters to God.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'They are wise scholars, nearly prophets in wisdom. If you are truthful, do not build what you will not reside in, and do not accumulate what you will not consume. And fear God, to whom you will return.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of true faith according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the profound link between theological conviction (Tawakkul and Ridha) and ethical conduct, characterizing the riders as 'wise scholars' whose intellect approaches prophetic insight. The Prophet’s advice to avoid building for the distant future or hoarding unused wealth reflects the Shia emphasis on *Zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as detachment from worldly accumulation in preparation for the Hereafter, a theme central to al-Saduq’s works on faith and deeds.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-175 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil Khat’tab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Bazi’a, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Azafer, on the authority of his father that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“God’s Prophet ran into a group of camel- riders during one of his trips. They greeted him and he asked them who they were. They said they were believers. The Prophet (MGB) asked them about the truth of their faith. They replied, ‘Contentment with what God has destined, entrusting themselves to God, and submitting to God’s orders.’ Then God’s Prophet (MGB) said, ‘These are wise and knowledgeable people with such a high rank, near that of the Prophets.’ Then he (MGB) faced them and said, ‘If you are truthful, do not build what you shall not reside in; do not collect what you shall not eat; and fear God to Whom you shall return.’”
